issues.legal_issue: In a suit for specific performance, readiness and willingness may be sufficiently averred and proved through the substance of the pleadings and the buyer’s conduct, without using a prescribed verbal formula.
material_facts: The buyer sued to enforce an agreement to sell property, with six months allowed for completion.

The plaint stated that the buyer was ready to complete the purchase, described repeated requests to the seller to execute the sale deed, and referred to a lawyer’s notice sent immediately after the completion period expired.
The buyer deposited the balance of the purchase price in court when filing the suit.
The trial court denied specific performance for failure to plead and prove continuing readiness and willingness, but the High Court granted the relief.
issues.conclusion: The pleadings and the surrounding conduct sufficiently established readiness and willingness; the High Court’s decree for specific performance was upheld and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, read with Explanation (ii), requires a plaintiff seeking specific performance to aver and prove that the plaintiff performed or was always ready and willing to perform the essential contractual obligations. Under Explanation (i), actual tender or deposit of money is not essential unless the court directs it. Readiness and willingness must be assessed from the substance of the pleadings as a whole and the relevant conduct and circumstances; no particular words or formula are required. The plaintiff must establish continuous readiness and willingness from the contract to the hearing. The Court relied on Ardeshir H. Mama v. Flora Sassoon, AIR 1928 PC 208, approved in Prem Raj v. D.L.F. Housing and Construction (Private) Ltd., AIR 1968 SC 1355; Chandiok v. Chuni Lal Sabharwal, (1970) 3 SCC 140; Syed Dastagir v. T.R. Gopalakrishna Setty, (1999) 6 SCC 337; Motilal Jain v. Ramdasi Devi, (2000) 6 SCC 420; and Surya Narain Upadhyaya v. Ram Roop Pandey, AIR 1994 SC 105.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and substantive_readiness_pleading and post_deadline_demand and repeated_completion_requests and balance_deposited_with_suit

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A buyer brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.substantive_readiness_pleading: The buyer’s pleading, read as a whole, conveyed readiness and willingness to perform the buyer’s contractual obligations.
predicates.post_deadline_demand: After the contractual completion period ended, the buyer sent a notice requiring the seller to execute the sale deed.
predicates.repeated_completion_requests: The buyer repeatedly met the seller and requested execution of the sale deed.
predicates.balance_deposited_with_suit: The buyer deposited the unpaid purchase price in court when filing the suit.

issues.definition: When a buyer seeking specific performance pleads readiness in substance and also makes repeated demands, gives notice after the completion period, and deposits the balance with the suit, the decree for specific performance is upheld.
